setup: Weight on the balls of your feet
Arms relaxed or hands on hips
execution: Bounce off the floor from your ankles
Touch down and spring straight back up
Knees nearly straight, heels off the floor
faults: Don't let your heels hit the floor
Don't bend your knees to jump higher

notes: Jump on a flat, forgiving surface in supportive shoes.
Start with low hops and a small number of contacts; build volume over weeks. The calves and Achilles area need time to adapt.
Stop the set when contacts get slow or heavy.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the shin, ankle or heel that builds
Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Low pogo jumps
regressions.reason: Tiny, quick hops that barely leave the floor.

regressions.name: Jump rope
regressions.reason: Similar small bounces at a steady rhythm.

progressions.name: High pogo jumps
progressions.reason: More height per hop with the same short contacts.

progressions.name: Single-leg hop
progressions.reason: One leg at a time; much higher load per leg.

progressions.name: Pogos forward or side to side

substitutions.name: Jump rope
substitutions.reason: Similar ankle work in longer rounds.

substitutions.name: Squat jump
substitutions.reason: Jump with more knee and hip bend.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at knee height, figure facing right, so the ankle bounce and the small knee bend are clear.

keyPositions.label: Contact
keyPositions.describe: Balls of the feet on the floor, heels just off it, knees almost straight, body upright and stiff like a spring.

keyPositions.label: Air
keyPositions.describe: A few centimetres off the floor, toes pointed down, legs nearly straight, body upright.
